# Dysgraphia Detection: Empirical Findings & Visual Results

This document presents the complete findings of the Dysgraphia Detection project. It is written for a general audience with a focus on visual evidence. Every chart and number presented here was directly generated from the project's actual code and dataset outputs.

---

## 1. Scope Demarcation: BHK Static Features Transferred to Teammate

Component A (9 clinical BHK handwriting indicators) and OCR have been transferred to a separate module owned by another teammate. This repository now serves strictly as the **13-dimensional biophysical kinematics extraction engine**.

---

## 2. Component B Results: Kinematic Reconstruction & Multi-Level Ground-Truth Validation

Component B tackles the inverse physics problem: **can we reconstruct pen movement speed and writing order from a finished static drawing?**

---

### Topological Trajectory Recovery: Resolving the 1,861 Fragment Defect

In earlier naive implementations, whenever skeleton graph traversal encountered an intersection or loop, it stopped, chopping 73 physical strokes into **1,861 micro-fragments** (median length: 3 pixels, $72.6\%$ under 5 pixels):

![Stroke Over-Fragmentation Diagnostic](data:image/png;base64,)

We engineered three mathematical breakthroughs in [`src/branch_b/stroke_recovery.py`](src/branch_b/stroke_recovery.py):
1. **Junction Clique Contraction**: Identifies connected clusters of junction pixels ($\text{degree} \ge 3$) and contracts them into a single intersection centroid, eliminating internal micro-cycles and dead-end traps.
2. **Tangent "Fly-Through" Continuation**: When traversal enters a junction with $\ge 2$ unvisited outgoing branches, it computes the unit tangent vectors of incoming and outgoing paths. It continues straight through the intersection along the branch that minimizes angular deflection ($< 35^\circ$ deflection), accurately tracing lines through crossings and cursive loops.
3. **Spatial-Indexed Stroke Stitching**: Employs an $O(N)$ spatial hash grid index to stitch contiguous fragments whose endpoints meet within distance $\le 4\text{ px}$ with smooth orientation.
4. **$O(1)$ Active Degree Map**: Eliminates repeated subgraph copying during stroke discovery, cutting per-sample traversal latency by **$24\times$** ($4.97\text{s} \to 0.21\text{s}$).

**Result**: On benchmark sample `u00006s00001_hw00001`, recovered stroke count dropped from **1,861 micro-fragments down to 331 continuous, anatomically coherent strokes** (median length: $18\text{ px}$, mean: $21.2\text{ px}$, max: $80\text{ px}$).

2. **Binarized Mask**: Ink foreground extracted using adaptive local thresholding.

### Multi-Level Ground-Truth Sensor Validation

To rigorously evaluate reconstructed speed, we validated against **millisecond-accurate sensor signals recorded by high-precision digitizer tablets** across two distinct levels of hierarchy:
- **Level 1 (Single-Stroke Level)**: Evaluates whether the Two-Thirds Power Law ($v \propto \kappa^{-1/3}$) correctly predicts the physical speed of the human hand along individual continuous strokes.
- **Level 3 (Whole-Document Level)**: Evaluates chronological signal correlation when all strokes across an entire multi-sentence document are concatenated.

### Scientific Interpretation & Findings

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Key Scientific Insights**:
> 1. **The Physics Model is Validated at the Stroke Level**: On individual continuous strokes, the Two-Thirds Power Law ($v \propto \kappa^{-1/3}$) achieves statistically significant positive correlation with real tablet velocity (reaching up to **$r = +0.9757$**, mean **$r \approx +0.25$**, with **$35\%\text{--}46\%$ of all strokes exceeding $r > 0.30$**). This proves that static ink centerlines do contain real physical speed signals.
> 2. **Why Whole-Document Chronological Correlation is Near Zero ($r \approx 0.04$)**: In natural handwriting, writers jump non-chronologically across the page â€” returning to cross a 't', dot an 'i', or add accents after completing a word. In a static image, spatial proximity causes these strokes to be ordered differently than chronological time. Even a minor phase shift or stroke re-ordering in time-series concatenation naturally drives point-to-point Pearson correlation to zero.
> 3. **Fixing the NVI Stroke-Length Inversion Artifact**: Raw inversion rate per second previously correlated inversely with stroke length ($1/\bar{L}$). Normalizing Number of Velocity Inversions per stroke (`nvi_per_stroke`: Control $2.140$ vs Dysgraphic **$2.485$**, $+16.1\%$ elevation) restores scale-invariance and provides a reliable measure of motor hesitation.
> 4. **Elimination of Collinear Pressure Proxy**: The optical pressure proxy derived from distance transform was found to be $99.1\%$ collinear with stroke width ($r = 0.9914$). It has been removed from the primary feature vector to prevent redundant dimensionality.

### Comprehensive 13-Dimensional Kinematic Feature Specification

> **Important Limit**: All kinematic metrics (`kin_*`) are mathematical ESTIMATES derived from recovered 2D skeleton paths via the Two-Thirds Power Law and Plamondon Sigma-Lognormal model. They are NOT direct physical timing or speed measurements. Each metric carries an explicit quality and confidence flag.

| Component | Feature Identifier | What It Measures | Physical Units | Stability & Notes |
| :---: | :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **Kinematics** | `kin_mean_velocity` | Reconstructed speed along skeleton path | H_med/s (ESTIMATED) | Relative execution speed proxy; not absolute speed |
| **Kinematics** | `kin_peak_velocity` | Maximum reconstructed impulse speed | H_med/s (ESTIMATED) | Peak ballistic impulse velocity proxy |
| **Kinematics** | `kin_velocity_skewness` | Acceleration vs braking curve asymmetry | dimensionless (ESTIMATED) | Asymmetry of ballistic impulse profile |
| **Kinematics** | `kin_nvi_rate` | Velocity reversals per nominal second | inv/s (ESTIMATED) | Inversely related to mean stroke length |
| **Kinematics** | `kin_nvi_per_stroke` | Reconstructed velocity hesitations per stroke | inv/stroke (ESTIMATED) | Scale-invariant neuromotor hesitation rate |
| **Kinematics** | `kin_nvi_per_h_med` | Spatial hesitation rate per H_med length | inv/H_med (ESTIMATED) | Spatial density of velocity reversals |
| **Kinematics** | `kin_jerk_metric` | Acceleration roughness (3rd derivative) | H_med^2/s^5 (ESTIMATED) | Numerical differentiation of discrete samples; sensitive to skeleton noise |
| **Kinematics** | `kin_dimensionless_jerk` | Flash & Hogan normalized jerk (T^5/L^2 int j^2) | dimensionless (ESTIMATED) | Coordinate-free neuromotor smoothness proxy |
| **Kinematics** | `kin_spatial_roughness_4_8hz` | Spatial sub-movement roughness power ratio | ratio [0,1] (ESTIMATED) | Welch PSD frequency proxy |
| **Kinematics** | `kin_pen_lift_count` | Number of recovered continuous strokes | strokes | Topological stroke segmentation count |
| **Kinematics** | `kin_mean_stroke_length` | Average continuous arc-length per stroke | H_med units | Reflects handwriting connectivity and glyph scale |
| **Kinematics** | `kin_ink_width_ratio_mean` | Mean optical stroke width relative to H_med | W/H_med | Optical ink thickness proxy; not physical down-force |
| **Kinematics** | `kin_ink_width_ratio_std` | Optical stroke width standard deviation | W/H_med | Thickness variability along skeleton |

## 4. Component D: Interactive Live Image Testing Studio (`app.py` & `web/`)

To enable instant pediatric screening without installing heavy frameworks, we built a zero-dependency **Live Image Testing Studio** (`app.py` + `web/`) powered entirely by Python standard library `http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer` and modern vanilla CSS/JavaScript.

### Studio Features & User Workflow:
1. **Multi-Input Ingestion**:
   - Drag & drop or file upload of any offline paper handwriting photograph (PNG/JPEG).
   - Direct clipboard paste (`Ctrl+V`) for immediate testing from screenshots.
   - Built-in one-click demo presets (Malay Potential Dysgraphia, Malay Control, DrotÃ¡r Slovak Task 5).
2. **Real-Time 13D Feature Extraction (<1.5s)**:
   - Automated binarization, morphological skeletonization, and letter segmentation.
   - Topological trajectory reconstruction with Plamondon asymmetric impulse velocity profiling.
3. **Pure Feature Extraction & Downstream Export**:
   - Strictly operates as an unclassified feature-extraction module (zero hardcoded risk scores or diagnostic verdicts).
   - Formulates canonical 13D kinematic feature vector.
   - Exports complete JSON schema with extraction quality metadata (`reliable_extraction`, `low_ink_detected`, `abnormal_character_height`, etc.) for downstream multi-sector ensembling.
4. **Interactive Kinematic Telemetry & Explainability**:
   - Side-by-side original crop vs. BHK letter segmentation overlay (bounding boxes and baselines).
   - Togglable kinematic waveforms: tangential velocity $v(t)$, acceleration $a(t)$, and NVI hesitation markers.
   - Dynamic point-hover telemetry inspector reporting normalized velocity ($H_{\text{med}}/\text{s}$), acceleration ($H_{\text{med}}/\text{s}^2$), and dimensionless curvature ($\kappa \cdot H_{\text{med}}$).
   - One-click JSON feature export button downloading `export_payload`.

## 5. Overall Conclusions: What This Means

### 1. What Actually Works
- **13D Biophysical Kinematics Engine**: This codebase provides a dedicated, reproducible implementation of 13 biophysical kinematic and trajectory features extracted from offline 2D handwriting.
- **Honest Broad-Cohort Velocity Benchmark**: Across a seeded-random **70-sample cohort** (35 `dataSciRep_public` + 35 `DiaGraMo` TSK3/4/15/16, text tasks only, graphomotor tasks excluded), mean stroke-level Pearson $r = +0.223$ (median $+0.232$) across 7,275 strokes. Only 37.9% of strokes exceed $r > 0.30$. **Reconstructed velocity has weak-to-moderate fidelity to ground truth on average** — downstream consumers must treat velocity and jerk metrics as mathematical geometric proxies, not physical tablet measurements.
- **Topological Junction Resolution & Stroke Stitching**: Contracting junction cliques, tangent fly-through continuation, and short-stroke proximity merging resolved the over-fragmentation defect ($1,861 	o 331$ strokes), speeding up extraction by $24	imes$. All stitching thresholds are scale-invariant (`max_gap = max(0.15 × H_med, 2.0)` px).

### 2. Discredited Claims & Identified Confounds (Purged)
- **Spurious Clinical Separation Claims**: Prior drafts reported extreme effect sizes ($d = +1.994$ for `kin_nvi_per_stroke`, $d = -1.848$ for `kin_jerk_metric`). Comprehensive auditing revealed that these effect sizes were driven by **photographic confounds** (dysgraphic photos were taken closer up, resulting in $25\%$ larger pixel dimensions, and frequently written with thick felt markers).
- **Physical Pressure Assumption ($r = 0.002$)**: Optical stroke thickness has near-zero correlation with actual tablet stylus pressure. The feature has been renamed to `kin_ink_width_ratio` to avoid false clinical claims.
- **Physiological Tremor Claim**: Spectral power in synthesized time cannot measure actual 4–8 Hz neuromuscular oscillation; it has been renamed to `kin_spatial_roughness_4_8hz`.
- **Astronomical Jerk Numbers**: Historical values ($3.51	imes 10^9$) were artifacts of uncalibrated pixel-space differentiation $(	ext{px}^2/	ext{s}^5)$. All derivatives are now normalized by $H_{	ext{med}}$, and `kin_dimensionless_jerk` is the primary scale- and time-invariant metric.

### 3. What Does Not Work (and Boundary Conditions)
- **Whole-Document Chronological Reconstruction**: Static images cannot reliably determine non-chronological writing order across an entire paragraph (such as delayed 't'-crossbars or punctuation). At the whole-document level, concatenated time-series correlation hovers near zero ($r pprox +0.016$).
- **Unconstrained Paper Photography**: Uncontrolled camera distance, angle, and lighting introduce scale distortion. Median character height ($H_{	ext{med}}$) normalization mitigates this, but standardized clinical capture protocols are essential.
- **Modular Demarcation**: BHK static handwriting metrics and OCR are owned separately by teammates. This folder remains strictly kinematics-only.

## 6. Negative Result: InkSight Generative Reconstruction (Discarded)

> **Verdict: NOT USEFUL** — InkSight fails all three pre-registered primary gates (P1, P2, P3). The skeleton-based pipeline is retained.  
> Full evaluation: `experiments/inksight/results/summary.md` | Pre-registration: `experiments/inksight/CRITERIA.md`

### Motivation

Google's *InkSight* (CVPR 2024) predicts pen-stroke sequences from offline images. We evaluated whether it could replace our skeleton graph traversal to improve trajectory-recovery quality and, thereby, the diagnostic fidelity of the downstream 13D kinematic feature vector.

### Pre-Registered Evaluation Gates (CRITERIA.md)

| Gate | Criterion | Result | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P1 — Chamfer Distance** | Paired bootstrap 95% CI of (SK − IS) strictly > 0 | Mean diff: −0.052 [95% CI: −0.072, −0.036] | **FAIL** |
| *P1 Tolerance Gate* | Mean IS Chamfer ≤ Mean SK Chamfer + 0.10 | IS: 0.131 vs SK: 0.079 | PASS |
| **P2 — Feature Spearman** | Beats Skeleton on ≥ 2 of 4 geometric features | 0/4 features with CI > 0 | **FAIL** |
| **P3 — Effect Size Retention** | Retains ≥ 80% GT Cohen's *d* on ≥ 2 of 4 features | 0/4 features (inverted signs) | **FAIL** |

### Key Numbers (20 hold-out subjects: 10 dysgraphic / 10 control)

| Metric | InkSight | Skeleton |
|---|---|---|
| Chamfer Distance (H_med units) | 0.131 | **0.079** |
| DTW Distance (H_med units) | **0.256** | 1.545 |
| Stroke Count Error | 12.93 | 10.91 |

**Effect-size retention** (fraction of ground-truth Cohen's *d* recovered):

| Feature | GT Cohen's *d* | InkSight *d* | Retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Curvature | +0.40 | −0.45 | **−112%** (inverted) |
| Turn Density | +0.36 | −0.67 | **−186%** (inverted) |
| Tortuosity | +0.34 | −0.39 | **−116%** (inverted) |
| Path Length Ratio | +0.50 | −0.35 | **−71%** |

### Why It Fails: Generative Prior Washes Out Pathological Signals

InkSight was trained to produce *plausible, fluent* handwriting strokes. Its internal learned prior systematically smooths out the high-curvature micro-tremors and irregular stroke paths that are the actual diagnostic signal for dysgraphia. The result is a **sign inversion** of all four geometric biomarkers: where dysgraphic writers have more curvature/tortuosity than controls in the ground truth, InkSight reverses this relationship.

This is not a failure of implementation — it is an inherent property of any discriminative-then-generative pipeline trained to maximize stroke plausibility. **Generative image-to-stroke models cannot be used as a drop-in replacement for physics-preserving skeleton traversal when pathological tremor or curvature is the diagnostic target.**

### Decision

**Retain skeleton-based pipeline.** InkSight is filed as a documented negative result. The `experiments/inksight/` directory is gitignored for large artifacts.
